s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive facial asymmetry with skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement
salient_findings: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement of the right side of the nose and cheek
Slightly hyperplastic soft tissue with dilated patulous follicles
key_facts: 10-year history of progressive symptoms
Multiple nondiagnostic skin biopsies
Septorhinoplasty 6 months prior due to collapse of the right nasal ala
Significant submucosal tissue was noted and removed from the right nasal cavity during surgery
Initial improvement after surgery, followed by enlargement of soft tissue and thickening of the overlying skin
Clinical examination revealed hyperplastic soft tissue and dilated patulous follicles
Surgical pathology showed fibroadipose tissue and vascular proliferation
Skin biopsy was interpreted as sebaceous hyperplasia
Surgical specimens revealed subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density
Thickened and fragmented collagen bundles were observed
Mature adipocytes extended into skeletal tissue
Spindle cells had bland cytomorphology with tapered nuclei and ill-defined cytoplasm
No cellular pleomorphism was observed

shortlist.label: Fibrolipomatous hamartoma
shortlist.why_kept: Subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue matches the clinical and pathological findings

shortlist.label: Madelung disease
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement, particularly on one side of the face, are consistent with this rare condition

shortlist.label: Lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multiple lipomas or lipomatous growths could explain the subcutaneous tissue enlargement and skin thickening

shortlist.label: Nuchal-type fibroma
shortlist.why_kept: The presence of spindle cells with bland cytomorphology and thickened collagen bundles is consistent with this diagnosis

shortlist.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
shortlist.why_kept: The clinical presentation of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement, combined with the histological findings of spindle cells and collagen bundles, makes this a plausible diagnosis

raw.rationale: The presence of subcutaneous-based proliferation of spindle cells with varying density, thickened and fragmented collagen bundles, and mature adipocytes extending into skeletal tissue, along with the clinical history of progressive skin thickening and subcutaneous enlargement, are characteristic features of fibrolipomatous hamartoma.

rejected.label: Madelung disease
rejected.why: It typically presents with multiple symmetric lipomas, which is not consistent with the asymmetric presentation in this case.

rejected.label: Lipomatosis
rejected.why: It is characterized by the presence of multiple lipomas, which is not the primary finding in this case.

rejected.label: Nuchal-type fibroma
rejected.why: It typically presents as a fibrous mass in the nuchal region, which is not consistent with the facial involvement in this case.

rejected.label: Dermatofibrosarcoma protuberans
rejected.why: It is a malignant tumor that typically presents with a history of rapid growth and cellular pleomorphism, which is not observed in this case.
